newsitem.title: UK: UK alters plan to get EU to ease mad cow beef ban.
newsitem.headline: UK alters plan to get EU to ease mad cow beef ban.

text.p: Britain said on Tuesday it was redoubling efforts to get the European Union to ease a ban on its beef exports by revising a plan that would exempt herds certified free of mad cow disease.

EU vetinerary scientists last month rejected Britain's original proposal for an Export Certified Herds Scheme, saying they were concerned about the government's ability to identify and trace all cattle at risk from the fatal disease.
Agriculture Minister Jack Cunningham said the revised proposals took account of the criticisms and would be more restricted than originally proposed.

"Eligibility for the scheme would be more restricted than originally proposed, but it would still be open in principle to producers in all parts of the United Kingdom," Cunningham said in a written parliamentary answer.

He said that in parallel, the government was developing a new proposal for an export scheme based on the age of cattle, details of which would be announced after exploratory talks with the Brussels-based European Commission, the EU's executive arm.
"We have put our ideas to the Commission about both schemes, and will press them with equal vigour," Cunningham said.
The EU slapped a worldwide ban on British beef exports, after scientists found evidence in March 1996 that mad cow disease could be transmitted to humans as Creutzfeldt Jakob Disease.
EU scientists in June identified five weaknesses in the original British proposals but suggested the scheme would prove acceptable if amended.
